newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan construction straight bond yields rise.
newsitem.headline: Japan construction straight bond yields rise.

text.p: Secondary market yields on straight bonds issued by second-tier Japanese construction firms face upward pressure after two listed general contractors virtually went bankrupt in July, bond traders said on Wednesday.
Buyers are absent despite high yields, as investors have become increasingly wary of the health of construction companies' balance sheets, traders said.

Fujita Corp's 3.0 percent straight bond, which is due September 2001 and was rated triple B minus by the Japan Bond Research Institute (JBRI), was being offered at a yield of 9.43 percent on Wednesday, nearly 800 basis points above the four-year interest-rate swap (IRS) rate of around 1.58/1.62 percent, traders said.

A 4.5 percent straight bond issued by JDC Corp, which is due September 1999 and also rated triple B minus by JBRI, was offered at a yield of 9.40 percent, more than 800 basis points above the two-year IRS rate of around 1.00/1.04 percent.

"Investors have been shunning construction company bonds with low credit ratings since earlier this year. This tendency became even more pronounced after the recent collapse of two construction firms," said a trader at a Japanese brokerage house.
In early July, Tokai Kogyo Co, a Tokyo-based mid-sized general contractor, applied for court protection under the Corporate Rehabilitation Law with debts totalling 510 billion yen.

This was followed last Wednesday by an application for court protection by another mid-sized general contractor, Tada Corp. Tada's debts totalled 171.4 billion yen, exceeding its assets by 77 billion yen.
Financial institutions are avoiding investments in bonds with low credit ratings ahead of the introduction of the prompt corrective action (PCA) system in April 1998, traders said.
The PCA system will use capital adequacy ratios as a major gauge of the soundness of financial institutions.

It will classify corporate bonds with ratings of BBB or above under the same asset category as Japanese government bonds, municipal bonds and government-guaranteed bonds, according to Ministry of Finance guidelines.
